results.name: vector3d_angle_between
results.evidence: Computes dot(in_EAX,in_ECX) of two Vector3D, early-outs to 0 when the vectors are componentwise equal, clamps the dot to [-1,1] and feeds it (via three call sites to FUN_00628140, a float10-returning helper consistent with an acos wrapper) to produce an angle.
results.summary: Returns the angle in radians between two 3D vectors passed in EAX/ECX, clamping the dot product to the valid acos domain.

results.name: vector3d_build_perpendicular
results.evidence: Picks the axis of in_EDX with smallest magnitude (comparing |x|,|y|,|z|) and forms an orthogonal vector in in_ECX by zeroing that axis and cross-multiplying the other two, the standard 'arbitrary perpendicular vector' construction.
results.summary: Given a direction vector in EDX, writes to ECX an arbitrary vector guaranteed to be perpendicular to it.

results.name: vector3d_rotate_about_perpendicular_axis
results.evidence: In-place update of *in_EAX using cross(in_ECX,in_EAX)*param_1 + in_EAX*param_2 — the sin/cos terms of Rodrigues' rotation formula but missing the axis*(axis.dot(v))*(1-cos) term that the full version (0x4cd820) includes, implying the caller guarantees axis⊥v.
results.summary: Rotates the vector at EAX around the axis at ECX by a given sin/cos pair, using the simplified formula valid only when the vector is already perpendicular to the axis.

results.name: vector3d_rotate_pair_in_plane
results.evidence: Applies a 2x2 Givens-style rotation simultaneously to the two vectors at in_EAX and in_ECX using shared sin/cos parameters (ECX'=cos*ECX+sin*EAX, EAX'=cos*EAX-sin*ECX), consistent with rotating a pair of orthogonal basis vectors together.
results.summary: Rotates two vectors (e.g. a pair of orthonormal basis axes) together within their shared plane by the given sin/cos angle.

results.name: vector3d_rotate_about_axis
results.evidence: Implements the full Rodrigues rotation formula: out = axis*(axis.dot(v))*(1-cos) + v*cos - cross(v,axis)*sin, matching param_1/param_2 as sin/cos; called from 29 sites, consistent with a core, widely used rotation primitive.
results.summary: Rotates the vector at EAX in place about the axis at ECX by the angle whose sine is param_1 and cosine is param_2.

results.name: vector3d_lerp
results.evidence: Computes *in_EAX = param_1*(*in_ECX) + (1-param_1)*(*in_EDX) componentwise for 3 floats, the textbook linear-interpolation formula.
results.summary: Linearly interpolates componentwise between two 3D vectors (ECX, EDX) by factor param_1, writing the result to EAX.

results.name: real_lerp_clamped
results.evidence: Blends param_1 and param_2 by factor param_3 (fVar1 = param_2*param_3 + (1-param_3)*param_1) then clamps the result to [0.0, 1.0] before storing through in_ECX.
results.summary: Linearly interpolates between two scalars and clamps the result to the [0,1] range, writing it through the ECX output pointer.

results.name: vector3d_rotate_toward_by_max_angle
results.evidence: If dot(ESI,ECX) already exceeds threshold param_2, copies ECX straight into the output (already within the cone); otherwise builds the cross(ECX,ESI) axis, guards against a degenerate (near-zero-length) axis by substituting an arbitrary perpendicular (FUN_004cd670), then calls the rotate-about-axis primitive (FUN_004cd820) with param_1/param_2 as sin/cos to turn ESI toward ECX by the limited angle.
results.summary: Rotates a source direction (ESI) toward a target direction (ECX) by at most the angle given by sin/cos params, returning whether a rotation was needed.

results.name: vector3d_project_onto_unit_axis
results.evidence: Computes fVar1=dot(in_EDX,in_ECX) then scales in_ECX by fVar1 directly (no division by |axis|^2), which is only correct if in_ECX is already unit length; optionally also outputs the perpendicular remainder via unaff_ESI.
results.summary: Splits vector EDX into components parallel and perpendicular to a (caller-guaranteed unit) axis ECX, writing the parallel part to EAX and optionally the perpendicular remainder to ESI.

results.name: vector3d_project_onto_axis
results.evidence: Computes dot(in_EDX,in_EDX) as the axis' squared length and divides by it before scaling, the general (non-unit-axis) vector projection formula; zero-length axis is special-cased to return a zero projection.
results.summary: Projects the vector at unaff_ESI onto the (arbitrary-length) axis at in_EDX, storing the projection in in_ECX and the perpendicular remainder in unaff_EDI.

results.name: quaternion_normalize
results.evidence: Sums the squares of the 4 floats at in_ECX (x,y,z,w) and, if positive, scales all 4 by 1/sqrt(sum); otherwise resets to the identity quaternion (0,0,0,1).
results.summary: Normalizes the quaternion at in_ECX in place, falling back to the identity quaternion when its length is zero.

results.name: quaternion_to_axis_angle
results.evidence: Copies the xyz part of the quaternion at in_EAX to the axis output, then computes 2*atan2(|xyz|, w) via fpatan for the angle, and mirrors the axis/angle (angle = 2pi-angle) when the result exceeds pi to keep the angle canonical.
results.summary: Converts the quaternion at EAX into an axis (written to ESI) and angle in radians (written to *EDI).

results.name: quaternion_multiply
results.evidence: Implements the standard Hamilton product formula on two 4-float quaternions (ECX, EAX) into EDX, with explicit local copies made first when the destination aliases either source operand.
results.summary: Multiplies two quaternions (ECX * EAX order per the formula) and writes the result to EDX, safely handling operand/destination aliasing.

results.name: quaternion_lerp
results.evidence: Negates the interpolation factor when dot(in_ECX,in_EDX) < 0 (shortest-path correction) then blends the 4 components linearly (param_1*ECX + (1-param_1)*EDX) into unaff_ESI — normalized-lerp rather than slerp (no trig).
results.summary: Performs a shortest-path linear (nlerp-style) interpolation between two quaternions (ECX, EDX) by factor param_1, writing the result to ESI.

results.name: quaternion_rotate_vector
results.evidence: Matches the well-known optimized quaternion-vector rotation identity: out = v*(2w^2-1) + q_xyz*2*dot(q_xyz,v) + cross(q_xyz,v)*2w, with param_1 the quaternion and in_ECX the vector.
results.summary: Rotates the 3D vector at in_ECX by the quaternion param_1, writing the rotated vector to in_EDX.

results.name: vector3d_build_orthonormal_basis
results.evidence: Passes the 3 components of in_EAX by value to FUN_004cba10 and receives back two separate 3-float outputs, which it copies into unaff_ESI and extraout_EDX — consistent with deriving a pair of vectors orthogonal to (and from) an input direction.
results.summary: Wraps a helper that derives two output vectors from an input direction vector, likely constructing tangent/bitangent-style basis vectors.

results.name: point3d_distance_squared_to_segment
results.evidence: Computes t = dot(EDX-EAX, ECX)/dot(ECX,ECX) clamped to [0,1] (closest point along the segment EAX+t*ECX to point EDX) then returns the squared length of the residual vector, the classic point-to-segment distance formula.
results.summary: Returns the squared distance from point EDX to the line segment starting at EAX with direction ECX, clamping the projection parameter to [0,1].

results.name: segment3d_distance_squared_to_segment
results.evidence: Full pattern match to Ericson's ClosestPtSegmentSegment algorithm: cross(dir1,dir2) near-zero epsilon test for the parallel case, clamped s/t in [0,1], degenerate-endpoint fallback that calls FUN_004cde30 (point-to-segment distance) on each endpoint, and a final squared-distance-of-residual return.
results.summary: Computes the squared distance between the closest points of two 3D line segments, handling the parallel/degenerate cases.

results.name: ray_intersects_sphere
results.evidence: Classic ray-sphere test structure (Real-Time Collision Detection's IntersectRaySphere): oc=origin-center, b=dot(oc,dir), early reject when moving away and origin outside sphere, discriminant test, and outputs the hit normal/point plus a t parameter.
results.summary: Tests a ray (origin in_EAX, direction in_EDX) against a sphere (center param_1, radius param_2), returning the hit t (via unaff_EDI) and surface normal (in_ECX) on success.

results.name: ray_intersects_cylinder
results.evidence: Solves the 2D (xy-plane) quadratic for a ray against an infinite cylinder of radius param_2, checks the hit's height falls within [0,param_1] and otherwise falls back to the sphere test FUN_004ce3a0 against the end cap, matching a capped-cylinder/capsule intersection routine.
results.summary: Tests a ray against a finite cylinder (with a spherical cap fallback), writing the hit fraction and point on success.

results.name: ray_intersects_sphere_test
results.evidence: Same discriminant math as FUN_004ce3a0/FUN_004ce7d0 (oc, b, discriminant against radius param_1) but only returns a boolean hit flag with no output point/normal/t.
results.summary: Boolean-only ray/sphere intersection test against a sphere of radius param_1, returning whether the ray hits without computing hit details.

results.name: ray_intersect_sphere_distance
results.evidence: Same ray-sphere discriminant setup as the boolean variant, but returns the near intersection distance (-b-sqrt(disc))/a as a float10, or FLT_MAX (3.4028235e38) as a sentinel for no hit.
results.summary: Computes the ray-parameter distance to the nearest intersection with a sphere of radius param_1, or FLT_MAX if the ray misses.

results.name: triangle3d_compute_barycentric_coordinates
results.evidence: Builds the triangle's normal via cross product, tests the query point's (unaff_ESI) plane distance squared against an epsilon-scaled |normal|^2 to reject off-plane points, then projects onto the dominant 2D plane (indices picked via the DAT_0065c29c/29e lookup table) to solve for two barycentric-style output coordinates.
results.summary: Given a triangle (EAX,ECX,EDX) and a point on its plane (ESI), computes two barycentric-style coordinates (param_1,param_2) describing the point's position on the triangle, using axis-dropping 2D projection for numerical stability.

results.name: segment3d_within_radius_of_segment
results.evidence: Reuses the same closest-point-between-segments structure as FUN_004cdef0 but compares the resulting squared distance against param_2^2 and returns a boolean, falling back to FUN_004ce6c0 (sphere/ray boolean test) at segment endpoints in the degenerate parallel case.
results.summary: Tests whether two 3D segments come within radius param_2 of each other, i.e. a segment-vs-thick-segment (capsule-like) proximity test.

results.name: plane3d_test_swept_sphere_range
results.evidence: Computes dot(EDX-ECX, normal EAX), tests it against a [-param_1, param_1+param_2] band, then evaluates a quadratic combining param_3/param_4 against the squared direction length before returning a boolean — consistent with a swept-sphere-vs-plane-band style test, though the exact geometric meaning of param_3/param_4 is not certain from this code alone.
results.summary: Performs a bounded-distance/quadratic test likely used to check whether a moving sphere or cone stays within a plane-relative band; low confidence on exact semantics.

results.name: plane3d_intersect_three
results.evidence: Computes the scalar triple product of the three plane-normal rows (param_1, unaff_EBX, unaff_EDI) as a determinant, rejects near-zero (parallel/degenerate) via a 1e-4 epsilon, then forms a weighted sum of cross products of the normals scaled by each plane's d component and divides by the determinant — exactly Cramer's-rule formula for the intersection point of three planes.
results.summary: Computes the single point where three planes (param_1, and two register-passed planes) intersect, returning false when the planes are parallel/degenerate.

results.name: plane3d_intersect_pair_to_line
results.evidence: Computes cross(in_EDX,unaff_ESI) as a candidate line direction (in_ECX) for the two planes, rejects a near-zero result (parallel planes) via a 0.0001 epsilon, then derives a point on the line using a weighted cross-product combination divided by the direction's squared length.
results.summary: Computes the line of intersection (direction in ECX, a point on it in EDI) of two planes given in EDX and ESI/EDI, returning false if the planes are parallel.

results.name: real_seek_towards_bounded
results.evidence: Maintains a position (unaff_EDI) and velocity (unaff_ESI) that are advanced toward target param_1 subject to a max-speed/accel-like pair (param_2,param_3) and clamped/wrapped into the range [param_4,param_5] depending on flag in_DL, matching a damped tracking/seek update rather than a pure clamp.
results.summary: Advances a tracked scalar value and its velocity toward a target, clamped (and optionally wrapped) to a [param_4,param_5] range — used for smoothly seeking a value such as an aim or turn angle.

results.name: vector3d_random_point_in_cone
results.evidence: Samples a disc radius via sqrt(2*random*param_3) clamped to param_2 (uniform-disc sampling), offsets a base direction (unaff_EDI) by a perpendicular vector of that length, then optionally rotates the offset around the base axis by a random angle (fcos/fsin fed into the rotate-about-axis primitive FUN_004cd820) — the standard cone-scatter construction used for e.g. weapon spread.
results.summary: Generates a randomly deviated direction vector within a cone around a base direction (unaff_EDI), used for angular spread/inaccuracy sampling.

results.name: byte_lerp_scan_threshold
results.evidence: Fetches a starting byte count from FUN_006391b4() then walks it downward while (byte/255)-lerp(param_1,param_2) stays above param_3, returning the first (or highest) byte index whose interpolated value is at or below the threshold; the only function in this batch with a clean 3-float __cdecl-style stack signature and no hidden register arguments.
results.prototype: unsigned char __cdecl byte_lerp_scan_threshold(float lo, float hi, float threshold)
results.summary: Finds the largest byte value (0-255) such that lerp(lo,hi,byte/255) is at or below the given threshold, scanning down from a count returned by FUN_006391b4.
